name: animated-frameworks
title: Animated Frameworks
description: A compatibility card with React, Next.js and HTML5 tiles that lift and tilt in 3D one after another. A faint circuit path behind them carries a travelling blue pulse, with a heading and blurb underneath.
use: A devtool landing page needs a compact card that names the frameworks or stacks it supports.
avoid: The three tiles and their icons are fixed, so showing other tools means editing the component, and the lift is tiny.
a11y: The looping lift and pulse ignore reduced-motion, and the framework icons have no text alternative beyond the description. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A tall dark card holding three rounded square tiles in a row, each with a small white framework glyph, over a faint corner-to-corner circuit line. A heading and two lines of grey text sit at the bottom.
behaves: The tiles take turns lifting, tilting back and moving toward the viewer over a slow cycle, while a soft blue glow travels along the circuit path behind them. The text stays still.
customise: The heading and description are props. The three framework tiles, their icons, the colours and the looping timing are fixed in the source.
weight: light: Three tiles with CSS transforms, one SVG pulse and a chain of timers; no per-frame JS.
demo: Heading Universal Compatibility with a line saying it works with React, Next.js and plain HTML.
issues: The travelling circuit pulse is so faint on the dark card that it barely reads.
The 3D lift is only a few pixels, so the stills look almost identical.
polishWhy: Neat three-tile card, but the lift and pulse are too faint to notice and it never stops.
